title: The Frame Matters More Than the Picture
author: Dominic Salles
summary: In this chapter of his Head of Department Manifesto, Dominic Salles argues that how something is framed shapes how it is valued and how the person doing it behaves. He opens with the story of offering free teacher training to local schools and finding almost no takers, concluding that free was the wrong frame. Citing Bartlett's example of renaming a sales team "partnerships", he says a new name changes the worker's own behaviour but only improves outcomes when paired with a focus on measurable impact, which most education relabelling lacks. He then turns the idea into a practical system for teaching assistants renamed Teaching Partners, who carry a caseload of ten to fifteen students, run experiments against each student's top three barriers over 6 to 12 weeks, and use a scaffolding checklist from correcting through to written scaffolds. A 14-question leadership checklist across time, beliefs and habits, curriculum and teaching, and management is applied to a retrieval practice initiative. The chapter ends by urging heads of department to lead upwards, since many senior teams have less experience running large, accountable departments.
points: Offering something for free signalled low value to schools, showing that framing can undermine a good offer before anyone sees its content.
Renaming a role only helps if the new name is paired with a checklist of actions and measures of impact; relabelling alone has never improved learning.
Teaching Partners should work a caseload of 10 to 15 students, identify each student's three greatest barriers, and run 6 to 12 week experiments on them.

A four-item review checklist and a graded scaffolding checklist (correcting, modelling, clueing, prompting, then visual, verbal and written scaffolds) keep the work simple enough to use in the moment.
Running a new initiative through 14 questions in about 15 to 20 minutes yields a fuller plan than the hours of discussion most schools give CPD, and heads of department can use it to lead upwards.
quotes: If it is free, it must be worth less. Or, if it is free, there must be a catch. Free was entirely the wrong frame. Frame things wrongly and no one will buy into your leadership message.
What will I write in my email, or say or offer that is a partnership, in which we all improve? The frame will actually change what I do and say.
Each name change in education means well. None of them improves learning and progress. Only one thing does. Focus on impact.
Whatever you try, don’t expect it to work first time. Find where it doesn’t work, and try to improve it.
One of the dangers of checklists is that they include too much. They don’t help in the moment because they are too long.
A checklist doesn’t remove your autonomy or sideline your professional expertise, it asks you to use that expertise in order to be much better at your job.
In real life, I only ask myself one question: If we do X, what impact will it have on progress?
Think back to the last bit of CPD or initiative in your school. Did it have anywhere near the amount of thought in how it was going to succeed?
The law of averages simply means that you are at least as capable as most of your SLT.
